The Sower
SOH-er
noun phrase
From the Greek speirō, “to sow,” the husbandman who casts seed; the parable of the four soils in which the seed is the Word of God.

Biblical Definition

The parable of the Sower stands first among the parables of the kingdom, and the LORD Himself called it the key to the rest: Know ye not this parable? and how then will ye know all parables? (Mar 4:13). A sower went forth to sow, and the seed fell upon four kinds of ground (Mat 13:3). Some fell by the way side, and the fowls came and devoured it up; some upon stony places, where it sprang up quickly but withered for want of root; some among thorns, which sprang up and choked it; and other fell into good ground, and brought forth fruit, some an hundredfold, some sixtyfold, some thirtyfold (Mat 13:4-8). The seed is the word of the kingdom (Mat 13:19), and the soils are the hearts of men that hear it. He that received seed into the good ground is he that heareth the word, and understandeth it; which also beareth fruit (Mat 13:23). The dictionary marks this parable as the great teaching on the Word and the heart. The same seed is cast on every ground, yet only the good ground bears fruit; and the good ground is not made good by itself, for by nature the heart is stony and thorny and trodden hard. So the Scripture teaches that fruit springs only where sovereign and effectual grace has prepared the soil, breaking up the fallow ground and giving the increase. The Word is the appointed means; the new heart is the gift of God; and the fruit, in patience, is the certain mark of the regenerate (Luk 8:15).

Webster 1828 Definition

The parable in which a sower casts seed on four soils, picturing the Word received in hearts prepared by sovereign grace.

expand to see more

THE SOWER, the parable of the four soils, first and chief of the kingdom parables.

The sower casts seed, which is the word of the kingdom, upon every kind of ground.

Three soils — the way side, the stony, the thorny — bear no abiding fruit.

The good ground heareth, understandeth, and bringeth forth fruit thirty, sixty, and an hundredfold.

The good ground is the heart prepared by effectual grace to receive the Word.

Key Scripture

Mat 13:3 — "And he spake many things unto them in parables, saying, Behold, a sower went forth to sow;"

Mar 4:13 — "And he said unto them, Know ye not this parable? and how then will ye know all parables?"

Mat 13:23 — "But he that received seed into the good ground is he that heareth the word, and understandeth it; which also beareth fruit, and bringeth forth, some an hundredfold, some sixty, some thirty."

Luk 8:15 — "But that on the good ground are they, which in an honest and good heart, having heard the word, keep it, and bring forth fruit with patience."

Modern Corruption

A parable of the kingdom plainly teaching that fruit springs only where grace prepares the heart; it has drawn little redefinition.

expand to see more

The parable of the Sower has drawn little redefinition from the present age, surviving as a familiar and beloved teaching of the LORD. The dictionary records it that the reader may mark the Word as the appointed seed and the prepared heart as the good ground in which alone it bears fruit.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is that the same Word falls on every heart, yet bears fruit only in the good ground, and the good ground is the heart that sovereign grace has prepared. The way side, the stony, and the thorny are not made fruitful by better sowing or by their own resolve; the increase is God’s. So the Scripture humbles the hearer and casts him upon the grace that gives both the seed and the soil; and it bids him take heed how he hear, for the abiding fruit, brought forth with patience, is the certain mark of a heart renewed by the LORD.

Hebrew Roots

From the Greek for “to sow,” the Sower names the parable of the four soils and the Word of the kingdom.

expand to see more

The Sower — from the Greek speirō, “to sow.”

A sower went forth to sow the word of the kingdom.

The seed fell on the way side, the stony, the thorny, and the good ground.

Only the good ground brought forth fruit, thirty, sixty, and an hundredfold.

The good ground is the heart prepared by effectual grace.

Usage

"Like the seed in the parable of the Sower, the Word bears fruit only in the good ground that grace has prepared."

"He that received seed into the good ground heareth the word, and understandeth it, and beareth fruit."

"Take heed how ye hear, for the fruit borne with patience is the mark of a heart renewed."
